name: Ogma v0.3.4
body:
### Project Switching and Draft Recovery
- Improved recovery of unsaved requests, notes, findings, workflows, environment variables, and settings when navigating, switching projects, or reopening Ogma.
- Prevented delayed saves, background results, and tool transfers from changing the wrong project or overwriting newer edits.
- Made interrupted creation and import operations safer to retry without creating duplicate sessions, findings, rules, or other resources.
- Added clearer recovery choices when competing drafts exist, and retained local edits when saved data cannot be read or a save cannot be confirmed.

### WebSocket Testing
- Added automatic detection and structured inspection of MessagePack and SignalR WebSocket messages, including SignalR traffic used by Blazor applications.
- Added decoded-message editing in Intercept and WebSocket Replay, with messages re-encoded for sending while preserving binary values and protocol fields.
- Improved WebSocket Replay connection cancellation, disconnect handling, transcript recovery, and live scrolling. Saved captured conversations are no longer limited by the visible timeline window.
- Improved live WebSocket and SSE history refreshes while keeping selected messages and events available as new traffic arrives.

### Certificates and Proxy Setup
- Added per-instance CA imports from password-protected PKCS#12/PFX and JKS bundles, or PEM/DER certificate and private-key pairs, with identity preview and selection.
- Added password-protected PKCS#12 CA exports alongside existing certificate downloads and backups.
- Improved embedded-browser certificate and proxy-authentication handling when changing a listener's CA, and made occupied proxy-port errors easier to understand.
- Fixed upstream proxy routing across target-facing tools and improved handling of saved proxy credentials.
- Added optional YAML startup configuration for repeatable listener, certificate, project, scope, and plugin setup.

### Replay
- Added editable, saved request pipelines with sequential, last-byte synchronization, and HTTP/2 single-packet strategies, plus inspection of saved pipeline runs.
- Improved attempt evidence so the effective request sent and any received response data remain available, including partial replies from interrupted exchanges.
- Preserved unsent request edits when duplicating sessions, exporting collections, or sending requests and selected attempts to Automate.
- Corrected multipart and URL-encoded form editing, preserving empty fields, Unicode text, file contents, and line endings when switching editor modes.
- Preserved exact JSON numbers, duplicate headers, and binary differences when editing or comparing requests and responses.

### Workflows and Automate
- Added a Shell workflow node for running local commands and passing their output to later steps, with captured output and execution diagnostics.
- Added Convert workflow processing for Automate extractor values, including values used by sequential runs.
- Improved workflow cancellation, timeouts, interrupted-run recovery, and live status when logging is disabled.
- Kept workflow edits and node positions intact, saved pending changes before execution, and improved Automate start, pause, resume, and stop behavior without clearing accepted results during refreshes.

### HTTP History, Search, and Sitemap
- Stabilized live traffic updates, filtered pagination, inspected-row loading, and scroll anchors in large HTTP histories. Refreshes retain accepted rows and the current viewport.
- Fixed original request-body display, response-body completion, and saving complete captured response bodies.
- Improved copied requests and exports to preserve captured paths, transport, Host overrides, empty headers, cookies, and body bytes more accurately.
- Kept Search results and Sitemap content visible during background refreshes or retryable failures, and corrected Sitemap parameter counts and IPv6 URLs.
- Preserved scope rate limits during import and export, and improved scope previews, activation feedback, and recovery after failed refreshes.

### Browser, Startup, and Updates
- Improved embedded-browser startup, proxy readiness, tab selection, popups, and navigation error reporting.
- Fixed stalled browser commands and HTTP authentication prompts interfering with subsequent actions, and preserved text composition while entering credentials.
- Improved startup recovery around occupied internal ports, unavailable log storage, and interrupted startup metadata writes.
- Changed Linux AppImage packaging to reduce CPU-heavy decompression during launch.
- Made update installation safer on Windows and Linux, preserving the installed AppImage if replacement fails and checking DEB installation after dependency repair.

### MCP, AI Assistant, and Plugins
- Improved task-oriented MCP tool discovery and loaded assistant tool descriptions on demand to reduce unnecessary context.
- Kept MCP actions and assistant conversations tied to their originating project, and stopped cancelled assistant operations from continuing with late tool calls or output.
- Improved AI request analysis for binary data, encoded WebSocket messages, and incomplete body previews.
- Improved plugin installation compatibility, settings recovery, and log refreshes, and corrected SDK request URLs and finding lookups for captured traffic.

### Files, Exports, and Utilities
- Improved hosted-file uploads, content editing, pagination, and recovery of interrupted saves without replacing newer selections or edits.
- Removed an implicit export row limit, made older backups reachable through pagination, and improved export progress and retry behavior.
- Preserved workflow dependencies and Automate wordlist references when importing projects.
- Corrected Unicode and binary comparisons, several Decoder conversions and validation checks, and token extraction from encoded responses.
- Improved OAST live counts and filtering, retained reverse-shell sessions through temporary connection loss, and expanded translated recovery messages and keyboard handling.

name: Ogma v0.3.3
body:
### Startup and Session Recovery

- Fixed outdated cached interface files causing blank screens or missing pages after an application update, without clearing saved preferences.
- Verified that the local API belongs to the newly launched backend before opening the workspace, rather than accepting a response from another process using the same port.
- Added recovery when a previous desktop backend still holds the proxy port after an interrupted session, without terminating unrelated applications.
- Fixed closing the main window leaving Ogma running when a standalone browser or another auxiliary window remains open. Temporary-session and unsaved-request confirmations are preserved.
- Improved startup errors to distinguish a backend readiness failure from a failure to load the interface.

### Database Reliability

- Prevented concurrent database connections from applying the same migration twice by checking the schema version after acquiring the write lock.
- Kept migration changes and schema-version updates in the same transaction, with automatic rollback on failure.

### Replay Notes

- Saved pending Replay notes before changing sessions, switching projects, or leaving Replay.
- Preserved newer note edits while earlier saves finish, and retained unsaved drafts with retry feedback when a save fails.
- Kept note saving functional when browser local storage is unavailable, using in-memory drafts and backend persistence.

### In-App Updates

- Added an accessible in-app release-notes dialog and retained release messages while an update downloads or waits to be installed.
- Increased the release-note limit from 4,000 to 120,000 characters so longer changelogs remain readable inside Ogma.
- Prevented background checks from overwriting a downloaded update or starting competing checks, and prevented repeated clicks from starting multiple downloads.
- Displayed actual download and installation errors, with a retry action for failed downloads.
- Enabled in-app updates for installed Linux DEB packages alongside Windows NSIS and Linux AppImage builds. DEB installation requires administrator authorization; restarting to install remains an explicit user action.
- Added a clear manual-update explanation and a GitHub Releases button for Windows portable, Linux unpacked, and unsigned macOS builds, while keeping version checks and release notes available.
- Checked macOS signing asynchronously and cached the result, so unsigned or ad-hoc-signed builds do not offer an installation path they cannot use. Automatic macOS updates require a properly signed application and its matching ZIP payload.

### Build and Validation

- Generated the required Windows and macOS update manifests after all platform builds, preserving architecture-specific metadata and validating referenced assets. Public release publication remains manual, without transferring installers through Actions artifact storage.
- Updated frontend dependencies and expanded regression coverage for startup recovery, cached interface upgrades, Replay notes, update progress, manual downloads, and architecture-specific update selection.

name: Ogma v0.3.2
body:
## v0.3.2

### Startup and Session Recovery 

- Fixed temporary sessions shutting down immediately after a slow database migration because the desktop lease had already expired.
- Gave saved projects the same startup allowance as temporary sessions so larger database migrations can finish before readiness times out.
- Bounded readiness polling, prevented duplicate retries, and stopped polling promptly when the backend fails or the session closes.
- Stopped the backend after failed startup readiness and prevented canceled startup operations from continuing after the window closes.
- Improved error reporting for inaccessible project directories and unexpected backend exits, including exits with code zero.
- Fixed development startup resource paths and authenticated desktop session save and discard requests.

### Sitemap and Database Performance 

- Added visible loading feedback and progressive rendering for large Sitemap flow graphs instead of building the entire graph in one blocking operation.
- Cached project sitemap results and reused path filters, folder totals, and host request counts to reduce repeated work while browsing graph pages.
- Allowed sitemap data to load independently of scope settings and discarded stale project and parameter results after navigation changes.
- Removed parameter-query joins that multiplied intermediate rows and improved indexed lookups for sitemap parameters and test verdicts.
- Added an index for response-body search document updates and reused prepared SQL statements during parameter capture.

### Replay, Intercept, and Automate 

- Prevented canceled Replay body loads from replacing the content of a newly selected request.
- Fixed intercepted request edits that removed query parameters being sent without an explicit query override.
- Preserved Automate filters and run ownership during asynchronous actions, and discarded endpoint-to-Automate handoffs after project switches.
- Stopped and drained Automate producers before clearing project data, preventing background runs from repopulating cleared records.
- Protected active Automate sessions during deletion and prevented new runs from slipping through while project cleanup is in progress.

### Workflows, Findings, and Match & Replace

- Preserved workflow edits made while a save is pending and prevented unrelated workflow deletions or delayed detail responses from replacing the current draft.
- Prevented stale workflow details from reversing a newer enable or disable action.
- Stopped autosaved workflow tests when newer edits remain unsaved, rather than testing an older definition as though it were current.
- Preserved newer finding edits and Match & Replace drafts when earlier save requests finish.

### Search, Scope, and Project Actions

- Made scope previews and captured-traffic counts use the backend's matching rules for consistent results.
- Kept scope and saved-filter deletion confirmations tied to the original selection when users navigate before confirming.
- Restored structured Search filters received from navigation actions and preserved request selection when activating or closing search tabs.
- Prevented repeated project creation while a creation request is already pending.
- Prevented delayed file-list responses from restoring deleted hosted files and kept discovery-job polling active when older requests finish late.

### Embedded Browser, MCP, and Plugins

- Preserved the embedded browser's active tab across delayed updates and synchronized loading indicators when switching tabs.
- Fixed MCP request repetition to preserve untouched duplicate query parameters, original encoding, and empty query segments while safely encoding replacement parameters.
- Corrected MCP URL overrides containing a query without a preceding slash, including IPv6 targets.
- Made browser WebSocket frame retrieval read the most recent matching messages and accurately report truncated results.
- Initialized the plugin SDK bridge on standalone plugin pages and advanced plugin event cursors past delivered events to avoid repeated delivery.
- Made the AI assistant consume queued request analysis when it opens and corrected conversation action button structure.

### Settings, Updates, and Utilities 

- Added live updater download progress in About settings and prevented delayed status snapshots from overwriting newer update events.
- Serialized timeout and custom-code preference updates, preserved newer JavaScript and rendering edits during delayed saves or initialization, and prevented obsolete custom-code activation after project changes.
- Kept AI settings saves tied to the submitted values and discarded connection-test results made obsolete by newer changes.
- Required TLS bypass hosts to finish loading before replacement saves, prevented overlapping TLS diagnostics, and retained newer certificate deletion confirmations.
- Validated custom scanner regular expressions with the backend engine rather than rejecting them using JavaScript's different syntax rules.
- Corrected IPv6 and socket-address validation for DNS settings and upstream proxy host patterns.
- Rejected malformed hexadecimal byte pairs and JWT headers or claims that are not JSON objects.

name: Ogma v0.3.1
body:
## v0.3.1


### Languages and Accessibility

- Added application translations in 24 languages, covering the interface, desktop dialogs, browser controls, workflow feedback, and exported security reports.
- Added a first-run language prompt, bilingual language names, and language-specific plural and number formatting.
- Added right-to-left layouts for supported languages while keeping URLs, protocol syntax, and technical viewers readable left to right.
- Improved keyboard navigation, modal focus handling, visible focus indicators, and translated layouts.

### HTTP History, Search, and Scope

- Added seek-based pagination, bounded table caches, and visible-page prioritization to reduce memory use and unnecessary work in large histories.
- Removed the loaded-row ceiling from filtered history browsing; additional results are fetched as needed rather than retained together in memory.
- Stabilized row selection, inspected requests, column sizing, and scroll position while new traffic arrives or background refreshes complete.
- Improved live reconciliation when responses change whether a request matches the active filter, including requests outside the currently loaded window.
- Fixed stale scope settings, show-all scope behavior, and manual HTTPQL queries being overwritten by header filters.
- Added the HTTPQL `is_null` operator for missing-response filters and corrected short Unicode body searches.
- Added pinned Search queries, HTTPQL field suggestions, and pagination controls for results beyond the first page.
- Added saved-filter import and export, and improved selected-request exports and history context actions.

### Replay, Automate, and WebSocket Testing

- Added project cookie jars with per-session selection in Replay.
- Made Match & Replace application optional for Replay requests and sequences, and added controls for preserving or recalculating Content-Length.
- Added per-session undo, request search, request-file saving, a GET/POST toggle, and target synchronization when pasting raw requests.
- Improved Replay tab shortcuts, request-draft preservation, and attempt selection when opening sessions.
- Added redirect following, response-side Match & Replace processing, payload alignment, a column picker, and bulk deletion in Automate.
- Added placeholder creation from selected request text and hexadecimal payload support.
- Improved WebSocket interception and browser message sending, prevented reconnects after an intentional disconnect, and bounded transcript rendering.
- Improved live SSE history refreshes, filtering, deletion, and WebSocket connection highlighting.

### Embedded Browser and Proxy

- Fixed the blank embedded-browser pane caused by an Electron rendering regression and updated Electron to 44.4.5.
- Added website HTTP authentication prompts and proxy-aware handling for authenticated WebSocket upgrades.
- Preserved connection-bound NTLM and Negotiate authentication and native popup contexts used by SSO flows.
- Added TLS client-certificate selection and ensured configured identities are presented to upstream targets and specialized probes.
- Added browser authentication controls and passkey account selection, with credential use restricted to trusted domains.
- Added optional per-instance proxy username and password authentication, with automatic credential handling in the embedded browser.
- Added a network-interface picker for proxy listener addresses and Linux transparent HTTP/HTTPS proxying gated on the required privileges.
- Preserved HTTP/2 request trailers during upstream forwarding and expanded HPACK regression coverage.

### Workflows and AI Assistant

- Added workflow creation and testing through AI assistant conversations.
- Added cross-workflow node copy and paste, HTTPQL preset filters, a resizable node configuration panel, and a full URL-encoding mode.
- Allowed structurally incomplete workflows to be saved while keeping validation feedback available for testing and execution.
- Reduced repeated graph serialization and polling updates, and improved node configuration and run-comparison state handling.
- Fixed project switching so Replay drafts are saved and Automate results, workflow execution details, Sitemap, and Search do not retain stale project state.

### MCP and Agent Workflows

- Added durable assessment checkpoints and a recovery timeline so agents can resume work after losing context.
- Added bounded tool discovery, exact contract lookup, compact Replay contracts, and actionable follow-up information while keeping the full tool list available.
- Updated MCP tool listings to preserve the protocol-required result type supplied by rmcp.
- Improved background-tab input, active-tab synchronization, browser snapshots, JavaScript dialogs, storage operations, and download metadata.
- Preserved primary finding evidence when linking supporting requests and added persisted WebSocket conversations for evidence workflows.
- Improved Match & Replace tool contracts, request-body searches, scope declaration, sitemap results, and long-running passive scan progress.
- Reduced redundant project lookups and browser health probes, and retained execution receipts across uncertain sends and session recovery.

### Project Data and Interface Reliability

- Improved project activation so stale list responses cannot restore the wrong active project.
- Added local-filesystem paths for saving and importing project backups, and a backup-management interface.
- Added Markdown and fullscreen finding descriptions, complete-project finding exports, and project-prefixed export filenames.
- Improved Sitemap navigation, path display, persisted expansion state, and endpoint details.
- Added collapsible navigation groups, additional appearance themes, shortcut import/export, and a CodeMirror editor for custom JavaScript and CSS.
- Reduced unnecessary allocations, repeated list refreshes, local-storage writes, and heavy syntax highlighting across the interface.
- Fixed stale plugin commands, file-upload and deletion state, export polling, scanner settings, and generated finding notifications.
- Improved startup progress, desktop window geometry, quit dialogs, and recovery from partially migrated databases.

### Build and Release

- Migrated application metadata to OgmaBox and updated compatible frontend and Rust dependencies.
- Bounded generated release notes so the first release in a new repository cannot exceed GitHub's description limit.
- Fixed retries to reuse existing draft releases instead of attempting to create them again.
- Restricted Linux capability helpers to Linux production builds while retaining cross-platform unit-test coverage, fixing the macOS and Windows compilation errors found during the v0.3.0 build.
